summary: Shoshone County, ID D-6 cupola lookout built 1919/20 or 1924 (sources differ); burned in a 1936 wildfire and not rebuilt; foundations and remnants remain on the peak.

facts.status_note: Destroyed by a 1936 wildfire and not rebuilt; a foundation and remnants remain on the site
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Panhandle National Forests

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site hike-in; a 2021 climbing guide describes a hike from Elsie Lake on trail FST-106, or a route from a road out of Osborn

events.note: Wallace Miner (May 29, 1919) reports a station will soon be established on Striped Peak, announced by the local Forest Service representative E. C. Pulaski
Register gives construction as 1919/20 and the built field as circa 1919
Everett H. Bryan named for 1920, citing a North Idaho Press item dated 07/02/1968; the citation date is later than the year, so the service date is unverified
Firelookout.com says built in 1924; the register photo is captioned circa 1924. Conflicts with the 1919/20 date
G. Richardson named for 1928, citing a Wallace Press-Times item dated 09/13/1928 (not read directly)
Spokesman-Review (July 11, 1929), quoted on Forest Lookouts: the Striped Peak lookout reported a fire near Marble Creek had virtually burned out
Destroyed in a wildfire in 1936 and not rebuilt; Firelookout.com calls it accidental burning
Registered February 28, 2021 as US 2069, ID 27; nominated by Brad Eells
Idaho Fire Lookouts post dated June 25, 2025 reports the D-6 foundation, a pit of remnants, a stacked rock foundation that may be a second building, and an unidentified memorial

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Four sources (register, Forest Lookouts, Firelookout.com, climbing guide) and Idaho Fire Lookouts' timeline date the wildfire loss to 1936. Idaho Fire Lookouts also quotes a book placing a lightning strike and burning in the 1960s; that account is second-hand and is not followed here.

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved: register says 1919/20 (built field circa 1919); Firelookout.com says 1924; register photo captioned circa 1924. Staffing entries for 1920 (Bryan, cited to a 1968 North Idaho Press item) and 1928 (Richardson, cited to a 1928 Wallace Press-Times item) come from Idaho Fire Lookouts; the newspapers were not read directly and the 1920 citation date needs a look. Elevation differs across sources: 6,300 ft (register), 6316 ft (Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts), 6,329 ft (1919 Wallace Miner). Forest name: register says Panhandle National Forests with Coeur d'Alene National Forest as cooperator; Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say Coeur d'Alene National Forest. Access comes from a 2021 climbing guide and Idaho Fire Lookouts' hike-in label; no closure or permit notice found. Facts omit a precise access level. The record's kind 'ground' and 1936 burned event are not contradicted. Register photo captions (1924 Forest Service photo, alidade photo) are not added as photos because no image URLs were read.
